title: Reference Sheet
subtitle: The SAT gives you this on every test — you never have to memorize it

blocks.html:
• Circle: area = πr². Circumference = 2πr.
  • Rectangle: area = ℓw (length times width).
  • Triangle area = × base × height.
  • Right triangle: a² + b² = c² (c is always the longest side, across from the right angle).
  • Circle has 360° of arc, or 2π radians, all the way around.
  • Angles in any triangle always add up to 180°.

• Move all the x's to one side, numbers to the other.
  • Combine like terms.
  • Divide to get x alone.
✏ EXAMPLE: 3 more than 8 times x is 83. 8x + 3 = 83 8x = 80 x = 10
✏ EXAMPLE: Solve: = 36 Multiply both sides by 25: x² = 900 Take the square root: x = 30 or x = −30

• "more than" / "increased by" → +
  • "less than" / "decreased by" → − (watch the order! "5 less than x" = x − 5)
  • "times" / "of" → ×
  • "per" / "each" → rate × variable
  • "is" / "equals" → =
✏ EXAMPLE: Oranges cost $3 per pound. Spent $27. How many pounds? Let p = pounds. 3p = 27 → p = 9
✏ EXAMPLE: 9 storage bins, same price each. A $63 coupon brings the total to $27. Price per bin? Let x = price per bin. 9x − 63 = 27 9x = 90 x = 10

title: Percent & Ratios
subtitle: Three patterns you'll see over and over

blocks.html:
• "What % of X is Y?" → percent = × 100
  • "What is P% of X?" → answer = (P ÷ 100) × X
  • "Y is P% more/less than X" → Y = X × (1 ± P ÷ 100)
✏ EXAMPLE: What percent of 300 is 75? (75 ÷ 300) × 100 = 25%
Ratios & proportions:
• Set up equal fractions and cross-multiply.
✏ EXAMPLE: Length:width = 35:10. Width grows by 7. How much does length grow? Ratio = = 3.5 New width = 10 + 7 = 17 New length = 17 × 3.5 = 59.5 Change = 59.5 − 35 = 24.5

title: Solving for One Variable in a Formula
subtitle: Plug in what you know first

blocks.html:
• Plug in the value you're given.
  • Solve like a normal one-variable equation.
✏ EXAMPLE: 2.5b + 5r = 80. If r = 16, find b. 2.5b + 5(16) = 80 2.5b + 80 = 80 2.5b = 0 b = 0
Elimination:

• Make one variable's coefficients match (or be opposites).
  • Add or subtract the equations to cancel that variable.
  • Solve, then plug back in.
✏ EXAMPLE: 24x + y = 48 and 6x + y = 72 Subtract: 18x = −24 x = = Plug into 6x + y = 72: −8 + y = 72 → y = 80
No solution vs. infinitely many:

• Same slope, different line (parallel) → NO solution
  • Same slope, exact same line → INFINITE solutions
✏ EXAMPLE: −3x + 21px = 84 has no solution. Find p. Rewrite: (21p − 3)x = 84 For no solution, the coefficient of x must be 0: 21p − 3 = 0 → p = =

• Plug the point into each inequality separately.
  • It's only a solution if it works for ALL of them.
✏ EXAMPLE: Is (8, 2) a solution to x > 0 AND y < 0? x = 8 > 0 ✓ y = 2 is NOT less than 0 ✗ Not a solution — fails the second inequality.

• m = slope = how steep the line is
  • b = y-intercept = where the line crosses the y-axis (value when x = 0)
  • Slope formula: m = =
From a slope + one point:

• y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)
  • Solve for y.
✏ EXAMPLE: Slope = , passes through (9, 10). y − 10 = (x − 9) y = x + 13
From a table of values:
✏ EXAMPLE: f(0) = 29, f(1) = 32, f(2) = 35 Slope = (32 − 29) ÷ (1 − 0) = 3 b = f(0) = 29 f(x) = 3x + 29
What slope means in real life:
✏ EXAMPLE: f(t) = 100 + 25t is money in a bank account after t deposits. What does 25 mean? 25 is the slope — the amount added EACH deposit. So: each deposit adds $25.

title: Quadratics & Parabolas
subtitle: x² equations and their U-shaped graphs

blocks.html: Factoring steps:

• Find two numbers that multiply to a×c and add to b.
  • Split the middle term using those numbers.
  • Group and factor. Set each factor = 0.
✏ EXAMPLE: x² + 5x + 6 = 0 Need two numbers: multiply to 6, add to 5 → 2 and 3 (x + 2)(x + 3) = 0 x = −2 or x = −3
Quadratic formula (when it won't factor):
Finding the vertex (min or max point):

• y = a(x − h)² + k → vertex is (h, k) — done, no work needed
  • y = ax² + bx + c → vertex x = , then plug in for y
✏ EXAMPLE: f(x) = (x − 10)(x + 13). Find the x of the minimum. Roots: x = 10 and x = −13 Vertex x is exactly in the middle: x = =
Discriminant = b² − 4ac tells you how many real answers:

DiscriminantMeaning
Positive2 real solutions
ZeroExactly 1 real solution
NegativeNo real solution
✏ EXAMPLE: −x² + bx − 676 = 0 has no real solution. b is a positive integer. Greatest possible b? b² − 4(−1)(−676) < 0 b² < 2704 b < 52 → greatest integer is 51

• a = starting value (where the graph crosses the y-axis)
  • b > 1 → growth. 0 < b < 1 → decay
✏ EXAMPLE: f(x) = 5,470(0.64) to the (x ÷ 12) power, x in months. Yearly % decrease? x ÷ 12 turns months into years, so 0.64 IS the yearly multiplier. Decrease = (1 − 0.64) × 100% = 36% per year

• xᵃ · xᵇ = xᵃ⁺ᵇ (same base, multiplying → add the powers)
  • (xᵃ)ᵇ = xᵃᵇ (power to a power → multiply)
  • A power means an n-th root: x^(1/n) = ⁿ√x
  • A negative power flips to a fraction: x⁻ⁿ =
✏ EXAMPLE: 2⁻³ = ? 2⁻³ = =
Solving an equation with a square root:

• Isolate the square root.
  • Square both sides.
  • Solve. Then check your answer in the original equation.
✏ EXAMPLE: √(x + 5) = 7 Square both sides: x + 5 = 49 x = 44
⚠ WATCH OUT: Squaring both sides can create a fake answer. Always plug your answer back into the ORIGINAL equation to double check.

• Drop the bars, write TWO equations: one positive, one negative.
  • Solve both.
✏ EXAMPLE: |x − 5| = 10 x − 5 = 10 → x = 15 x − 5 = −10 → x = −5
⚠ WATCH OUT: If the equation says |something| = a NEGATIVE number, there is NO solution. Absolute value can never be negative.
✏ EXAMPLE: 45-45-90 triangle: each leg is 6. Find the hypotenuse. Hypotenuse = leg × √2 Hypotenuse = 6√2
✏ EXAMPLE: 30-60-90 triangle: short leg (across from 30°) is 5. Find the other two sides. Long leg = short leg × √3 = 5√3 Hypotenuse = short leg × 2 = 10
✏ EXAMPLE: Isosceles right triangle has hypotenuse 58. Find the perimeter. leg = = 29√2 Perimeter = 29√2 + 29√2 + 58 = 58√2 + 58

• Pick an angle (not the right angle). Call it θ.
  • Hypotenuse = longest side, always across from the right angle.
  • Opposite = the side across from θ.
  • Adjacent = the side touching θ (that isn't the hypotenuse).

Memory hook

SOH-CAH-TOA (memorize this word):

• SOH: sin θ =
  • CAH: cos θ =
  • TOA: tan θ =
How to solve any SOH-CAH-TOA problem:

• Find θ (the angle you care about) and label the 3 sides from ITS point of view.
  • Decide which two sides you know or want (opp/hyp, adj/hyp, or opp/adj).
  • Pick SOH, CAH, or TOA to match those two sides.
  • Plug the numbers in as a fraction. That's your answer (or solve for the missing side).
✏ EXAMPLE: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4, hypotenuse 5. θ is opposite the side of length 3. Find sin θ, cos θ, tan θ. Opposite = 3, Adjacent = 4, Hypotenuse = 5 sin θ = cos θ = tan θ =
Complementary angle trick:

• The two non-right angles in a right triangle always add to 90°.
  • So: cos(one angle) = sin(the other angle)

✏ EXAMPLE: In triangle JKL, cos(K) = and angle J is the right angle. Find cos(L). K and L are complementary, so cos(L) = sin(K). Find the missing side with a² + b² = c²: 24² + b² = 51² → b² = 2601 − 576 = 2025 → b = 45 sin(K) = = So cos(L) =

• Find which vertices match up (the problem will tell you, like "P corresponds to S").
  • Matching angles are equal. Use "angles add to 180°" to find missing ones.

✏ EXAMPLE: Right triangles PQR ~ STU, P matches S. Angle Q = 18°. Find angle S. Angle R and angle U are the right angles (90° each). In triangle PQR: angle P = 180 − 90 − 18 = 72° Angle P matches angle S, so angle S = 72°
(x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² center = (h, k), radius = r
✏ EXAMPLE: x² + (y − 1)² = 49, shifted down 2. New equation? New center: (0, 1 − 2) = (0, −1) New equation: x² + (y + 1)² = 49
If it's not already in that form:

• Group x-terms and y-terms; move the constant to the other side.
  • For each group: half the middle coefficient, square it, add to both sides.
  • Rewrite each side as a perfect square.
Arc measure:
• Arc measure = its central angle. Arc RS = 100° → angle ROS = 100° (O = center).

title: Volume
subtitle: How much space a 3D shape holds

blocks.html:
ShapeVolume Formula
Box (rectangular prism)V = ℓwh
CylinderV = πr²h
SphereV = πr³
ConeV = πr²h
PyramidV = ℓwh
✏ EXAMPLE: Box: length 5, width 3, height 4. Find the volume. V = ℓwh = 5 × 3 × 4 V = 60 cubic units
✏ EXAMPLE: Cylinder: radius 3, height 10. Use π ≈ 3.14. V = πr²h = 3.14 × 3² × 10 V = 3.14 × 9 × 10 V = 282.6 cubic units

title: Surface Area
subtitle: The total area of all outside faces

blocks.html:
ShapeSurface Area Formula
BoxSA = 2(ℓw + ℓh + wh)
Cube (side s)SA = 6s²
CylinderSA = 2πr² + 2πrh
✏ EXAMPLE: Box: length 4, width 3, height 2. Find the surface area. SA = 2(ℓw + ℓh + wh) SA = 2(12 + 8 + 6) SA = 2(26) = 52 square units
Gluing two solids together:
• Faces that get glued together are no longer on the outside — subtract them twice (once from each solid).

✏ EXAMPLE: Two cubes, each with side 4, are glued together face-to-face. Find the combined surface area. One cube's surface area: 6 × 4² = 6 × 16 = 96 Two cubes separately: 2 × 96 = 192 Subtract the 2 glued faces (one from each cube): 192 − 2(16) = 160 Combined surface area = 160 square units

title: Parallel Lines & Angles
subtitle: A transversal crossing two parallel lines

blocks.html:
• Vertical angles (across from each other) are EQUAL.
  • Corresponding angles (same corner, different line) are EQUAL.
  • Same-side interior angles ADD UP TO 180°.
✏ EXAMPLE: Angle x = 65°. Find the corresponding angle y, and the same-side interior angle z. y is corresponding to x, so y = 65° z is same-side interior with x, so z = 180 − 65 = 115°

WordMeaningHow to find it
Meanthe averageadd everything up, divide by how many numbers
Medianthe middle valuesort the numbers, find the middle one
Modethe most common valuewhichever number shows up most
Rangethe spreadbiggest number minus smallest number
✏ EXAMPLE: Data set: 2, 3, 3, 5, 7 Mean = (2+3+3+5+7) ÷ 5 = 4 Median = 3 (the middle number) Mode = 3 (appears twice) Range = 7 − 2 = 5
⚠ WATCH OUT: If you add the same number to every value in a data set: mean and median shift by that amount, but range stays exactly the same.

Estimate p, margin of error m → the true value is PLAUSIBLY between (p − m) and (p + m).
✏ EXAMPLE: Estimate = 0.49, margin of error = 0.04. What's plausible? Range: 0.49 − 0.04 = 0.45 to 0.49 + 0.04 = 0.53 Plausible the true value is between 0.45 and 0.53.
⚠ WATCH OUT: The right answer always describes a RANGE — never says the value is "exactly" one number.
✏ EXAMPLE: Convert 5,104 yards to miles. (1 mile = 1,760 yards) 5,104 ÷ 1,760 ≈ 2.9 miles

• Find the category on the bottom axis.
  • Trace straight up to the top of that bar.
  • Trace across to the numbered side axis. That's your answer.

• Stuck? Try plugging in the answer choices, starting with B or C.

  • "Must be true" question? Test it with real numbers.

  • Double check your units.
